div.l: Lyk a staff / ther was no calf seene
Wel cowde he kepe / a gerner and a bynne
Ther was no Auditour / that cowd of him wynne
Wel wost he bi the drowhte and by the reyn
The yeldyng of his seed / and of his greyn
His lordys sheep / his neet his deyere
His swyn his hors / hys stoor / and his pultrye
Was holly / in this revys governyng
And bi couenaunt / yaf he reknynge
Syn that his lord / was xxᵗʸ wyntir of age
Ther coude no man / castyııı him in a rerage
Ther nas baylyf / ne herde / ne other hyne
That he ne knewe his sleyhte / and his covyne
They were a drad of him / as of the dethe
His wonyng was wol faire vppon an hethe
Wᵗith. grene trees shadwed / was his place
He coude bettir . than his lord / purchase
Wel ryche he was / astored pryvely
His lorde he covde wel please and sotelly
To yeve and lene him / of his owne good
And haue a thank / and yet a coote and an hoode
In youthe hadde he lerned / a good mister
He was a wol wryhte / and a carpenter
This Reve sat vpon a wol good stot
That was pomly grey / and hyhte scot
A surcote long / of pers vpon he hadde
And by his side / he bare arusty bladde
Of Northfold was this Reve / of which I tell
Biside a town / men clepyn baldyswelle
Tukked he was / as is a frer aboute
And evyr he rood / the hyndyrest of the rowte
A Sompnour was ther / wᵗith vs in that place Sompnour
That hadde a feyr reed cherubyn̄ is face
For sausflem he was wᵗith eyen narowe .
